subject: Genetics
title: Consent and Consumer DNA
description: A quick, practical guide to Consent and Consumer DNA.

hook.text: You sent spit to 23andMe for ancestry results. You didn't consent to police using your relatives' data to solve crimes.

buildup.text: Consumer DNA companies hold data on over 40 million people. Most terms of service allow law enforcement access.

discovery.text: GEDmatch changed its policy after the Golden State Killer case. Users now must opt in to law enforcement matching.

twist.text: But your consent doesn't protect your relatives. If your cousin opts in, your family tree is exposed regardless.

climax.text: Individual consent fails when DNA is shared biology. Your privacy depends on every relative's choices.

punchline.text: You opted out. Your cousin didn't. Too late.

quiz.question: Why doesn't individual consent fully protect DNA privacy?
options: Relatives' choices can expose your genetic data
